title: Iki action test (iki/v1)
description: A fixture in a plugin's tests/ directory: an action run on given values, and how it should end (ADR 0093). `iki plugin test` makes the run input the server would, runs it with `iki-worker run --local`, and compares what it writes.

apiVersion.description: The spec version this manifest follows.

name.description: What the test is called in its report. Unique in the plugin. The file's name, and the document's number if it holds several, unless given.

description.description: What the test checks, for whoever reads its report.

action.description: The plugin's action, by name, such as `compute_properties`.

upgrade.description: Use these inputs as database samples for the plugin's upgrade probe. Supply values that can be stored by the earlier build, including any required references.

after.description: Expected values after the upgrade, by input name and sample position. Each object names the fields to check on that sample.

params.description: Its params' values, as a person would give them. A file param names one of `files` as `{"$file": "name"}`.

settings.description: The plugin's settings for the run, over their defaults.

inputs.description: Each input's entities, in order. A file field's value names one of `files` as `{"$file": "name"}`.

type.description: Its type, if it's a subtype of the input's: `namespace/plugin.Type`.

request.description: For a request (ADR 0132): the project that asked, and the service it was sent to, as the server gives them (ADR 0232). The service is the test's project, `service`, unless given; null for a request not sent yet.

asking_project.description: The project that asked, which owns the request.

service.description: The service it was sent to, or null until it's sent.

included.description: For an input that includes references (ADR 0105): the entities each names, by reference. Each gets an ID, which the reference holds; one left out is an empty list.

type.description: Its type, if it's a subtype of the one the reference names.

files.description: The files the values and params name, each a path relative to the plugin's directory.

expect.description: How the run should end. With `output`, it succeeds and writes at least that; with `error`, it fails and says so. With neither, it only has to succeed.

output.description: What output.json should contain: each key given, each list's items in order. Keys left out aren't compared.

error.description: Text the command's last `::error` line should contain.

tolerance.description: How far a number may be from the one given, relative to it. 1e-9 unless given.

project.description: A project, as the other side's people see it.

hrid.description: Its HRID, if the command reads it. Made from the type's prefix unless given.
